what_this_is: The R-20 population of periodic/receipt_walk, the seventh of the fourteen to retire, enumerated from committed artifacts BEFORE this slice's first src/ edit, together with what a declaration of this family has to carry -- written down in advance so a short total is a stop rather than a discovery.

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97: the code lands against the committed baselines plus this allowlist, and no baseline moves inside the semantic commit.

qualifying_population.rule: R-20's second half. What can move is a property of which participants hold a declaring owner of the periodic family, which is a fact about the committed scenario set rather than about the diff, so the population is enumerated from committed artifacts -- docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json at e58594b, whose own fields are derived from the behaviour catalog and from scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json's scenario subtrees -- before the first src/ edit. Any occurrence outside it is an unexpected one and stops the slice exactly as an over-count would.
qualifying_population.predicate: Every committed coupled scenario that puts a declaring owner of the periodic family on a participant. The seven owners are read live from the behaviour catalog over rule_owners() -- Bami's Cinder, Blackfire Torch, Fated Ashes, Hollow Radiance, Liandry's Torment, Sunfire Aegis, Unending Despair -- which is the same family-to-owner join golden_snapshot.receipt_walk_families() makes for the coverage guard, so the population and the guard cannot disagree about which rosters can see the family.
qualifying_population.method: scripts.receipt_walk_schedule.population_size over each selected scenario subtree of the committed coupled baseline -- the whole scenario subtree, because a slice that moves a family's pricing can move any aggregate downstream of it inside that scenario.

pair_engine_population.why: scripts/golden_baseline.json is the one-attacker pair-engine surface, and this slice adds no pair-engine arithmetic: the two stamps it adds pair-side -- pair_preview_of on each cadence's row and the row's own declaration on the ticks under it -- are not leaves that baseline holds, which records each build's sorted breakdown_keys and its total_damage and neither a row's inner fields nor an event. Zero pair-engine golden diffs is therefore a declared population of zero rather than an observation, and a single diff there stops the slice.

qualifying_population.which_owners_the_population_can_actually: TWO of the seven, and between them they cover two of the three declared cadences. immolate_active_bruiser_roster puts Sunfire Aegis on the Darius, which is the CONTINUOUS_AURA shape; liandry_reprice_mage_roster puts Liandry's Torment on the Ahri, which is the REFRESHED_BURN shape AND the one packet of this family that an existing re-pricing site re-prices after authoring it. No committed coupled scenario holds Bami's Cinder, Blackfire Torch, Fated Ashes, Hollow Radiance or Unending Despair, so the third cadence -- FIXED_INTERVAL, declared by Unending Despair alone -- is outside the population entirely. That is recorded BEFORE the edit rather than discovered after it, and it is why this slice carries an equivalence fixture per owner in umbrella Amendment P's shape, which is what covers the third cadence and the four uncovered burns and auras.
qualifying_population.predicted: 0 occurrences inside a population of 2694. The walk's from-declaration price and the pair engine's are the same real number with the multiplications associated differently -- the pair engine mitigates and then applies the holder's magic amp, the walk composes the amp pre-mitigation and mitigates once (Amendment M, Ruling 1) -- so the two agree to within one unit in the last place, four orders of magnitude below the 0.005 golden equality grades to (R-13). The one site that re-prices a packet of this family moves the magnitude and the declaration is rescaled with it, so the resistance each side prices at is the same one. A leaf that did move could only move by 0.01, which qualifies under none of R-15's three tests.

what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.rule: Enumerated in advance, in the idiom the charged_strike and on_hit_strike slices used: writing down what the walk will have to read is what makes a wrong number a stop instead of a discovery.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.one_authoring_site_and_three_cadences: damage._add_burn_damage authors all three: a refreshed burn priced as a rate over the window the fight's casts stretched it to, a continuous aura priced as a rate times the fight, and a fixed-interval strike priced as one packet per completed interval. Each row is a single mitigated aggregate whose ticks damage._periodic_damage_events splits out of it, so the declaration is stated once at the row and each tick carries its share of it -- the same restatement damage._row_declaration_share makes for a coarse row, through the same one method on the declaration.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_magnitude_is_the_pre_mitigation_aggr: raw_burn already carries the burn multiplier the refresh window earned, raw_immolate already carries the fight duration, and raw_periodic already carries the proc count. All three are allocations of the cadence rather than amplifiers, the engine applies them pre-mitigation, and mitigation is linear -- so folding them into the declared magnitude prices to the same real number.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_attack_class_is_OTHER_for_all_seven: Measured rather than defaulted: every periodic row is priced by damage._mitigate and by nothing else, so no part amp is earned. All seven declare MAGIC, which makes the holder's static magic amp a live term for the whole family -- _mitigate multiplies magic damage by it whatever delivered it, and StaticHolderAmps.factor_for delivers it off the damage type alone, so a declaration that pre-multiplied it would be the undeclared second producer D-60 forbids.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_resistance_term_and_the_one_site_tha: damage._apply_liandry_reprice folds a raised maximum health back onto Liandry's own burn ticks after they are authored -- one of the three re-pricing sites umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 2's census enumerates, and the only one that touches a row of this family. It rescales the packet's MAGNITUDE rather than its mitigation, so what the declaration owes is a rescale and not a resistance: damage._carry_declarations_onto_repriced_ticks already carries each authored tick's declaration onto the tick that replaces it and rescales it by what that tick moved by. This slice is the first that arms that path, so liandry_reprice_mage_roster is the scenario where Ruling 1's kept-in-step half is exercised end to end.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_coarse_row_shape: A continuous aura whose declaration publishes no event interval authors no damage_events at all (damage._add_burn_damage stamps them only when source.event_interval is not None). The row still has to state its declaration, because the reconstruction then synthesizes one event per typed part and damage._row_declaration_share splits it the way the damage was split.

what_this_family_authors_that_this_slice.rule: The committed triage measures a family's authored pair rows by ITEM ablation, which is conservative by construction -- removing the item removes every mechanic it holds, not only the mechanic of this family. One of the eight rows it lists for periodic is authored by no declaration of this family, and recording that before the edit is what keeps a row that stays priced from reading as a half-performed retirement.
what_this_family_authors_that_this_slice.damage_amp_Liandry's Torment: The delta_amp family's own row -- liandrys_torment.whole_total_amp -- authored by damage._apply_general_amplifiers, which reads the ordered ledger and writes a derived bonus row beside it. Liandry's Torment declares two rules in two families, and only the burn is this one's.

why_the_family_is_startable_now.the_class: Class (a), authors-own-rows, in the committed triage (umbrella Amendment O, Ruling 2): seven declarations authoring seven priced pair-engine rows, so Amendment L, Ruling 1's shape has something to stamp and the row retires by the ruled act rather than by reclassification.
why_the_family_is_startable_now.the_standing_precondition: umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 2's source-derived term census is green -- python scripts/term_census.py --check reports 29 post-authoring packet-mutation sites, 0 uncovered, 3 static holder amps, 0 unfolded -- which is the standing precondition on any further family retiring.
why_the_family_is_startable_now.the_covering_scenarios: Amendment L, Ruling 2's prerequisite is met without an integration act, and Amendment N, Ruling 3's magic re-pricing scenario is one of the two: liandry_reprice_mage_roster was landed as an integration act precisely to arm the Liandry reprice, and this is the family whose row that reprice moves.

no_baseline_moves: R-32's five baselines are untouched by every commit of this slice. docs/behavior-frontier.json and docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json are machine-derived receipts whose counters this slice moves, so they move with it (R-36); holding them back would make the slice red against a gate it is forbidden to contain.
the_stage_fixture_moves_with_this_slice: umbrella Amendment L, Ruling 3 requires the from-declaration stage to carry an equivalence fixture 'on a family that has not yet opted in'. That fixture stood on this family -- Sunfire Aegis's immolate -- so this slice migrates it to spellblade's Bloodsong proc, which the pair engine still prices. A fixture left on a retired family would be the stage checking itself, which is the re-spelling claim turning into a tautology with a green tick on it. The fixture also gains the resistance field its packet meets, because the negative case has to perturb the one a physical packet actually met and perturbing the other would pass by testing nothing.

measured_after.golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. The declared pair-engine population of 0 held.
measured_after.coupled_golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. Zero of the 2694 enumerated leaves moved.
measured_after.oracle_receipts_owed: None. R-19 owes an investigator per qualifying occurrence (R-15) and there were none, in a population enumerated in advance and non-empty.
measured_after.what_the_walk_actually_priced: A zero on a baseline is evidence a family's numbers did not move; it is not evidence the walk priced anything. Read off survival.transitions.apply_declared_price itself over both covering scenarios: on immolate_active_bruiser_roster the walk priced EIGHT ticks of sunfire_aegis.continuous_aura, seven at a declared 31.5 and the drift-corrected last at 31.49999999999999, paying 18.862275449101794 and 18.862275449101787; on liandry_reprice_mage_roster it priced TEN ticks of liandrys_torment.refreshed_burn, paying 22.010159651669085 and 24.18722786647315. Every one of the eighteen equals the number the pair engine put on that same tick, one pricing per (mechanic, subject, event_id).
measured_after.the_reprice_is_the_one_that_matters: The last two Liandry ticks carry a declared 33.330000000000005 where the first eight carry 30.330000000000002. That difference is damage._apply_liandry_reprice folding a raised maximum health back onto ticks it had already authored, and damage._carry_declarations_onto_repriced_ticks rescaling the declaration on each tick it replaces. This is the first family whose packets an existing re-pricing site moves, so it is the first end-to-end exercise of umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 1's kept-in-step half -- on the scenario Ruling 3 landed as an integration act for exactly this term. A declaration left at its pre-lifeline magnitude would have deleted the reprice from every total holding it.
measured_after.the_five_owners_and_the_cadence_the_popu: Covered by the equivalence fixture the slice added per owner, in umbrella Amendment P's shape: a pair fight per declaring owner, holding an Abyssal Mask beside it so every packet is priced at a magic amp other than 1.0 -- which covers the whole family here rather than half of it, since all seven declare magic. Every tick is asserted equal to the pair engine's own number for it AND the ticks are asserted to sum to the row, so a cadence that split its aggregate wrongly fails there rather than shipping. Seven owners, all green, including the FIXED_INTERVAL cadence that Unending Despair declares alone and that no committed scenario holds.
measured_after.the_gate_the_population_could_not_bound: R-01 row 8 is green on all four bench scenarios with and without the compiled walk, and every winner and score is unchanged (cassiopeia_3champ 4003.1, cassiopeia_5champ 5010.8, mundo_3champ 3305.0, syndra_mandate_3champ 4642.3) with residuals 79 / 19 / 12 / 98.
